title: What CPNI training do the FCC rules require of telecom carriers?
description: How 47 CFR 64.2009 requires carriers to train staff on CPNI use, keep a disciplinary process, and file an officer's compliance certificate by March 1.
shortAnswer: The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) requires telecommunications carriers, including interconnected VoIP providers, to train their personnel on when they are and are not authorized to use customer proprietary network information (CPNI), and to have an express disciplinary process, under 47 CFR 64.2009(b). An officer must also sign and file an annual compliance certificate by March 1 explaining how the carrier's operating procedures ensure compliance.
keyTakeaways: Section 64.2009(b) requires carriers to train personnel on when they are and are not authorized to use CPNI and to have an express disciplinary process in place.

An officer with personal knowledge of the carrier's procedures must sign an annual compliance certificate, filed with the Enforcement Bureau in EB Docket No. 06-36 by March 1 for the previous calendar year (64.2009(e)).
Sales staff need supervisory approval for outbound marketing that requests customer approval, and carriers keep campaign and compliance records for at least one year.
Front line staff must authenticate customers before disclosing CPNI by phone, online or in store under 64.2010, which makes authentication the core practical training content.
A 2023 SIM change rule includes a specific employee training duty for wireless carriers, but as at November 2026 the eCFR text says compliance is not required until a compliance date is set.
jurisdiction: United States (federal): 47 U.S.C. 222 and 47 CFR Part 64, Subpart U
appliesTo: Telecommunications carriers, including local, long distance and wireless carriers
Providers of interconnected VoIP service, which the rules treat as carriers for CPNI purposes
Customer service, retail store and sales personnel who access or use CPNI
Officers who sign the annual CPNI compliance certificate
Agents and affiliates that handle CPNI on a carrier's behalf

sections.heading: What does 47 CFR 64.2009 require for CPNI training?

blocks.text: Carriers must train their personnel as to when they are and are not authorized to use CPNI, and they must have an express disciplinary process in place. That is the whole of the training sentence in [47 CFR 64.2009(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-64/subpart-U/section-64.2009), and it is short by design: the content of the training is defined by the rest of Subpart U.

blocks.title: The rule text
blocks.text: "Telecommunications carriers must train their personnel as to when they are and are not authorized to use CPNI, and carriers must have an express disciplinary process in place." 47 CFR 64.2009(b)

CPNI has the meaning given in section 222(h)(1) of the Communications Act, codified at [47 U.S.C. 222](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/47/222). The FCC's consumer guide describes it in practical terms as information such as the numbers a customer calls, when they call, and the services they use, such as call forwarding or voicemail. Under [47 CFR 64.2003(o)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/47/64.2003), the term carrier for Subpart U includes providers of interconnected VoIP service, so cloud voice businesses carry the same training duty as traditional carriers.

The rule does not set a frequency, a format or a minimum length. Because the officer must certify each year that operating procedures are adequate, most carriers run training at onboarding and at least annually, timed so completion data is available before the March 1 filing.

sections.heading: What other safeguards in 64.2009 depend on trained staff?

blocks.text: Section 64.2009 sets six safeguards, and four of them only work if staff know the procedure. Training content should follow each paragraph rather than treating CPNI as a general privacy topic.

items: **Approval status (a):** carriers must implement a system that clearly establishes a customer's CPNI approval status before CPNI is used. Staff must know where to check it and what to do when it is unclear.

**Campaign records (c):** carriers keep a record of their own and affiliates' sales and marketing campaigns that use CPNI, and of every disclosure of CPNI to third parties, for at least one year. Marketing staff need to know what must be logged.

**Supervisory review (d):** sales personnel must obtain supervisory approval of any proposed outbound marketing request for customer approval, with compliance records kept for at least one year. Supervisors need to know what they are approving.

**Opt out failures (f):** carriers must give the FCC written notice within five business days of any instance where opt out mechanisms do not work properly to the point that the problem is more than an anomaly. Staff who receive complaints need an escalation path that starts the clock.

sections.heading: What does the annual CPNI certification require?

blocks.text: Every year an officer, acting as an agent of the carrier, must sign and file a compliance certificate stating that he or she has personal knowledge that the company has established operating procedures adequate to ensure compliance with Subpart U. The filing is made with the Enforcement Bureau in EB Docket No. 06-36 on or before March 1, covering the previous calendar year.

Section 64.2009(e) requires three items with the certificate: a statement explaining how the carrier's operating procedures ensure that it is or is not in compliance, an explanation of any actions taken against data brokers, and a summary of all customer complaints received in the past year about unauthorized release of CPNI. The FCC's guide [Protecting Your Privacy: Phone and Cable Records](https://www.fcc.gov/consumers/guides/protecting-your-privacy) describes the same duty from the customer's side.

Training is the evidence most often cited in the accompanying statement, because it is how the carrier shows that procedures are known and followed. An officer who signs on "personal knowledge" should see completion rates, assessment results and disciplinary outcomes, not only a policy document. [How to report training compliance to the board](/guides/how-to-report-training-compliance-to-the-board) covers how to package that evidence.

sections.heading: Why is customer authentication the core of CPNI training?

blocks.text: Most CPNI incidents start at the point of contact, so the authentication rules in 64.2010 are the procedures front line staff use every day. Carriers must take reasonable measures to discover and protect against attempts to gain unauthorized access to CPNI and must properly authenticate a customer before disclosing CPNI on a customer initiated call, online, or in store.

blocks.text: Scenario based assessment fits these rules well, because the failure mode is social engineering rather than lack of awareness. See [how to design competency assessments](/guides/how-to-design-competency-assessments).

sections.heading: What do staff need to know about CPNI breaches and SIM change fraud?

blocks.text: Staff must know how to escalate a suspected CPNI breach immediately, because the carrier must electronically notify the United States Secret Service and the FBI as soon as practicable and no later than seven business days after reasonable determination of the breach. Under [47 CFR 64.2011](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/47/64.2011), the carrier generally may not notify customers or the public until seven full business days after that notice, and it must keep breach records for at least two years.

The FCC adopted amendments to 64.2011 published at 89 FR 10002 on February 12, 2024. As at November 2026, the eCFR shows those amendments as not yet incorporated into the current text, so the seven business day law enforcement process quoted above is still the operative rule. Carriers should confirm status with counsel before revising breach training.

For wireless carriers, 64.2010(h)(7) requires training that addresses fraudulent SIM change attempts, complaints and remediation, including how to identify potentially fraudulent requests, how to spot a customer who may be a victim of SIM swap fraud, and how to route both to specifically trained employees. Paragraph (h)(9) states that compliance with paragraph (h) is not required until it is removed or contains a compliance date, and as at November 2026 the eCFR still carries that statement. Building the module now avoids a scramble when a date is set.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each Subpart U paragraph to the roles it touches and to the assessment that evidences it, so the officer signing the March 1 certificate can trace every statement back to training records. When a pending rule such as the SIM change training duty takes effect, the affected roles and modules are already identified.

faqs.q: How often must CPNI training be repeated?
faqs.a: The rule sets no frequency. Section 64.2009(b) only requires that personnel be trained on authorized and unauthorized use. Because an officer certifies compliance every year, carriers commonly train at onboarding and annually, and retrain after a policy change, a system change affecting approval status, or a disciplinary finding.

faqs.q: Do interconnected VoIP providers have to follow the CPNI training rule?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 64.2003(o) states that for Subpart U the terms telecommunications carrier and carrier include an entity that provides interconnected VoIP service, as defined in 47 CFR 9.3. Those providers must train personnel, maintain a disciplinary process, and file the annual certification like any other carrier.

faqs.q: Who signs the CPNI compliance certificate?
faqs.a: An officer of the carrier, acting as its agent, who can state that he or she has personal knowledge that the company has established operating procedures adequate to ensure compliance. The certificate and accompanying statement are filed with the Enforcement Bureau in EB Docket No. 06-36 on or before March 1 each year.

faqs.q: Does CPNI training cover contractors and agents?
faqs.a: The rule says personnel, and carriers remain responsible for CPNI handled on their behalf. In practice, outsourced contact centers, authorized retail dealers and agents who access CPNI should receive the same authentication and use training, with completion evidence supplied to the carrier, so the certifying officer has a basis for the annual statement.
